flags.name: --model-path
flags.help: The path of the model weights. This can be a local folder or a Hugging Face repo ID.

flags.name: --tokenizer-path
flags.help: The path of the tokenizer.

flags.name: --tokenizer-mode
flags.help: Tokenizer mode. ‘auto’ will use the fast tokenizer if available, and ‘slow’ will always use the slow tokenizer.

flags.name: --tokenizer-backend
flags.help: Tokenizer backend. ‘huggingface’ uses the default HuggingFace tokenizers library; ‘fastokens’ uses the fastokens library for faster tokenization. Requires the fastokens package to be installed.

flags.name: --tokenizer-worker-num
flags.help: The worker num of the tokenizer manager.

flags.name: --skip-tokenizer-init
flags.help: If set, skip init tokenizer and pass input_ids in generate request.

flags.name: --load-format
flags.help: The format of the model weights to load. “auto” will try to load the weights in the safetensors format and fall back to the pytorch bin format if safetensors format is not available. “pt” will load the weights in the pytorch bin format. “safetensors” will load the weights in the safetensors format. “npcache” will load the weights in pytorch format and store a numpy cache to speed up the loading. “dummy” will initialize the weights with random values, which is mainly for profiling.”gguf” will load the weights in the gguf format. “bitsandbytes” will load the weights using bitsandbytes quantization.”layered” loads weights layer by layer so that one can quantize a layer before loading another to make the peak memory envelope smaller. “flash_rl” will load the weights in flash_rl format. “fastsafetensors” and “private” are also supported. “runai_streamer” enables direct model loading from object storage and shared file systems.

flags.name: --model-loader-extra-config
flags.help: Extra config for model loader. This will be passed to the model loader corresponding to the chosen load_format.

flags.name: --trust-remote-code
flags.help: Whether or not to allow for custom models defined on the Hub in their own modeling files.

flags.name: --context-length
flags.help: The model’s maximum context length. Defaults to None (will use the value from the model’s config.json instead).

flags.name: --is-embedding
flags.help: Whether to use a CausalLM as an embedding model.

flags.name: --enable-multimodal
flags.help: Enable the multimodal functionality for the served model. If the model being served is not multimodal, nothing will happen.

flags.name: --revision
flags.help: The specific model version to use. It can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default version.

flags.name: --model-impl
flags.help: Which implementation of the model to use. “auto” will try to use the SGLang implementation if it exists and fall back to the Transformers implementation if no SGLang implementation is available. “sglang” will use the SGLang model implementation. “transformers” will use the Transformers model implementation.

flags.name: --detokenizer-worker-num
flags.help: The worker num of the detokenizer manager.

flags.name: --prefill-only-disable-kv-cache
flags.help: Skip the physical KV cache allocation for embedding-mode prefill-only workloads. Currently only valid with —is-embedding, —chunked-prefill-size=-1, —disable-radix-cache, an FA prefill backend, and non-FP4 KV cache so the fa_skip_kv_cache path is active (no layer reads or writes the cache). Other prefill-only workloads such as scoring/MIS may benefit from this later once their attention paths stop using paged KV. Scheduler admission accounting is unchanged; per-layer K/V tensors are sized to (page_size, head_num, head_dim) placeholders so GPU memory is not wasted.

flags.name: --model-config-parser
flags.help: Which model-config parser to use. “auto” picks “mistral” via the is_mistral_model name heuristic, else “hf” (AutoConfig over config.json). Plugins can register additional parsers via @register_model_config_parser.

flags.name: --host
flags.help: The host of the HTTP server.

flags.name: --port
flags.help: The port of the HTTP server.

flags.name: --fastapi-root-path
flags.help: App is behind a path based routing proxy.

flags.name: --grpc-mode
flags.help: If set, use gRPC server instead of HTTP server.

flags.name: --skip-server-warmup
flags.help: If set, skip warmup.

flags.name: --warmups
flags.help: Specify custom warmup functions (csv) to run before server starts eg. —warmups=warmup_name1,warmup_name2 will run the functions warmup_name1 and warmup_name2 specified in warmup.py before the server starts listening for requests

flags.name: --nccl-port
flags.help: The port for NCCL distributed environment setup. Defaults to a random port.

flags.name: --checkpoint-engine-wait-weights-before-ready
flags.help: If set, the server will wait for initial weights to be loaded via checkpoint-engine or other update methods before serving inference requests.

flags.name: --ssl-keyfile
flags.help: The file path to the SSL key file.

flags.name: --ssl-certfile
flags.help: The file path to the SSL certificate file.

flags.name: --ssl-ca-certs
flags.help: The CA certificates file.

flags.name: --ssl-keyfile-password
flags.help: The password to decrypt the SSL keyfile.

flags.name: --enable-ssl-refresh
flags.help: Enable automatic SSL certificate hot-reloading when cert/key files change on disk. Requires —ssl-certfile and —ssl-keyfile.

flags.name: --enable-http2
flags.help: Use Granian instead of Uvicorn as the ASGI server, enabling HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 auto-negotiation. Clients may use h2c (cleartext HTTP/2) or plain HTTP/1.1. Requires ‘pip install sglang[http2]’.

flags.name: --http2-max-concurrent-streams
flags.help: Maximum number of concurrent streams advertised on each HTTP/2 connection (1 to 2^32 - 1). Only applies with —enable-http2.

flags.name: --dtype
flags.help: Data type for model weights and activations. * “auto” will use FP16 precision for FP32 and FP16 models, and BF16 precision for BF16 models. * “half” for FP16. Recommended for AWQ quantization. * “float16” is the same as “half”. * “bfloat16” for a balance between precision and range. * “float” is shorthand for FP32 precision. * “float32” for FP32 precision.

flags.name: --quantization
flags.help: The quantization method.

flags.name: --quantization-param-path
flags.help: Path to the JSON file containing the KV cache scaling factors. This should generally be supplied, when KV cache dtype is FP8. Otherwise, KV cache scaling factors default to 1.0, which may cause accuracy issues.

flags.name: --kv-cache-dtype
flags.help: Data type for kv cache storage. “auto” will use model data type. “bf16” or “bfloat16” for BF16 KV cache. “fp8_e5m2” and “fp8_e4m3” are supported for CUDA 11.8+. “nvfp4” selects the NVFP4 FP4 E2M1 KV cache recipe; “fp4_mx_block16” selects the block-size-16 FP4 E2M1 KV cache recipe. Both require CUDA 12.8+ and PyTorch 2.8.0+

flags.name: --enable-fp32-lm-head
flags.help: If set, the LM head outputs (logits) are in FP32.

flags.name: --modelopt-quant
flags.help: The ModelOpt quantization configuration. Supported values: ‘fp8’, ‘int4_awq’, ‘w4a8_awq’, ‘nvfp4’, ‘nvfp4_awq’. This requires the NVIDIA Model Optimizer library to be installed: pip install nvidia-modelopt

flags.name: --modelopt-checkpoint-restore-path
flags.help: Path to restore a previously saved ModelOpt quantized checkpoint. If provided, the quantization process will be skipped and the model will be loaded from this checkpoint.

flags.name: --modelopt-checkpoint-save-path
flags.help: Path to save the ModelOpt quantized checkpoint after quantization. This allows reusing the quantized model in future runs.

flags.name: --modelopt-export-path
flags.help: Path to export the quantized model in HuggingFace format after ModelOpt quantization. The exported model can then be used directly with SGLang for inference. If not provided, the model will not be exported.

flags.name: --quantize-and-serve
flags.help: Quantize the model with ModelOpt and immediately serve it without exporting. This is useful for development and prototyping. For production, it’s recommended to use separate quantization and deployment steps.

flags.name: --rl-quant-profile
flags.help: Path to the FlashRL quantization profile. Required when using —load-format flash_rl.

flags.name: --enable-quant-communications
flags.help: Enable INT8 quantization of TP communications (Supported only for NPU for Qwen3 series).

flags.name: --enable-tf32-matmul
flags.help: Enable float32 matmuls to use TensorFloat32 precision for better performance (via torch.set_float32_matmul_precision). CUDA only. Automatically enabled for MiniMax-M2 and GLM-4 models.

flags.name: --mem-fraction-static
flags.help: The fraction of the memory used for static allocation (model weights and KV cache memory pool). Use a smaller value if you see out-of-memory errors. When unset, it is computed as (GPU memory - reserved memory) / GPU memory, defaulting to 0.88 if GPU memory cannot be detected.

flags.name: --max-running-requests
flags.help: The maximum number of running requests.

flags.name: --max-queued-requests
flags.help: The maximum number of queued requests. This option is ignored when using disaggregation-mode.

flags.name: --max-total-tokens
flags.help: The maximum number of tokens in the memory pool. If not specified, it will be automatically calculated based on the memory usage fraction. This option is typically used for development and debugging purposes.

flags.name: --chunked-prefill-size
flags.help: The maximum number of tokens in a chunk for the chunked prefill. Setting this to -1 means disabling chunked prefill.

flags.name: --prefill-max-requests
flags.help: The maximum number of requests in a prefill batch. If not specified, there is no limit.

flags.name: --enable-dynamic-chunking
flags.help: Enable dynamic chunk size adjustment for pipeline parallelism. When enabled, chunk sizes are dynamically calculated based on fitted function to maintain consistent execution time across chunks.

flags.name: --max-prefill-tokens
flags.help: The maximum number of tokens in a prefill batch. The real bound will be the maximum of this value and the model’s maximum context length.

flags.name: --schedule-policy
flags.help: The scheduling policy of the requests.

flags.name: --enable-priority-scheduling
flags.help: Enable priority scheduling. Requests with higher priority integer values will be scheduled first by default.

flags.name: --abort-on-priority-when-disabled
flags.help: If set, abort requests that specify a priority when priority scheduling is disabled.

flags.name: --schedule-low-priority-values-first
flags.help: If specified with —enable-priority-scheduling, the scheduler will schedule requests with lower priority integer values first.

flags.name: --priority-scheduling-preemption-threshold
flags.help: Minimum difference in priorities for an incoming request to have to preempt running request(s).

flags.name: --schedule-conservativeness
flags.help: How conservative the schedule policy is. A larger value means more conservative scheduling. Use a larger value if you see requests being retracted frequently.

flags.name: --retraction-policy
flags.help: The decode retraction policy to use when the KV cache is full. ‘length’ preserves the existing behavior and retracts short-output, long-input requests first. ‘priority’ retracts lower-priority requests first, using the same priority direction as priority scheduling.

flags.name: --page-size
flags.help: The number of tokens in a page.

flags.name: --enable-page-major-kv-layout
flags.help: Store the Mamba state and full/SWA KV caches as one entry per token slot, holding every layer’s state, in a single page-granular buffer instead of one buffer per layer. Implied by --enable-unified-memory, and currently supported only with it.

flags.name: --enable-unified-memory
flags.help: For hybrid Mamba/GDN and hybrid SWA models, replace the statically-partitioned pools (full-attention KV + SWA/Mamba conv/SSM state) with a single byte buffer split dynamically between the sub-pools, so KV-vs-state capacity flexes with the workload instead of being fixed at startup. Implies --enable-page-major-kv-layout. Requires stride-aware attention, linear-attention and Mamba backends; the allowed backends and the supported PD-disaggregation and speculative-decoding configurations are validated at startup.

flags.name: --swa-full-tokens-ratio
flags.help: The ratio of SWA layer KV tokens / full layer KV tokens, regardless of the number of swa:full layers. It should be between 0 and 1. E.g. 0.5 means if each swa layer has 50 tokens, then each full layer has 100 tokens.

flags.name: --disable-hybrid-swa-memory
flags.help: Disable the hybrid SWA memory.

flags.name: --radix-eviction-policy
flags.help: The eviction policy of radix trees. ‘lru’ stands for Least Recently Used, ‘lfu’ stands for Least Frequently Used.

flags.name: --enable-prefill-delayer
flags.help: Enable prefill delayer for DP attention to reduce idle time.

flags.name: --prefill-delayer-max-delay-passes
flags.help: Maximum forward passes to delay prefill.

flags.name: --prefill-delayer-token-usage-low-watermark
flags.help: Token usage low watermark for prefill delayer.

flags.name: --prefill-delayer-queue-min-ratio
flags.help: Opt-in to the adaptive queue-based delay trigger (independent of the slot-based one). Defers prefill until the waiting queue reaches min(running_req * ratio, max_prefill_bs) so small fragments batch into a larger prefill. Unset keeps the original slot-only behavior. Typical: 0.1–0.5.

flags.name: --prefill-delayer-max-delay-ms
flags.help: Wall-clock cap (ms) on a single queue-trigger delay; once exceeded, prefill is force-released to bound worst-case TTFT. Only consulted when --prefill-delayer-queue-min-ratio is set. Typical: 1000–5000.

flags.name: --prefill-delayer-forward-passes-buckets
flags.help: Custom buckets for prefill delayer forward passes histogram. 0 and max_delay_passes-1 will be auto-added.

flags.name: --prefill-delayer-wait-seconds-buckets
flags.help: Custom buckets for prefill delayer wait seconds histogram. 0 will be auto-added.

flags.name: --disable-priority-preemption
flags.help: Disable priority scheduling preemption.

flags.name: --default-priority-value
flags.help: Default priority for requests without explicit priority.

flags.name: --device
flags.help: The device to use (‘cuda’, ‘xpu’, ‘hpu’, ‘npu’, ‘cpu’). Defaults to auto-detection if not specified.

flags.name: --tensor-parallel-size
flags.help: The tensor parallelism size.

flags.name: --pipeline-parallel-size
flags.help: The pipeline parallelism size.

flags.name: --attention-context-parallel-size
flags.help: The attention context parallelism size.

flags.name: --dcp-size
flags.help: The decode context parallelism size. See Decode Context Parallelism.

flags.name: --dcp-comm-backend
flags.help: Communication backend for the DCP attention reduction: AllGather + ReduceScatter, fused NCCL All-to-All, or FlashInfer MNNVL All-to-All. Unset resolves to fi_a2a where the DCP group shares an MNNVL domain on Blackwell, else a2a on CUDA/ROCm, else ag_rs.

flags.name: --dcp-replicate-q-proj
flags.help: For MLA DCP with the a2a/fi_a2a backend: replicate the Q projection so each DCP rank computes the full-head query locally. Use —no-dcp-replicate-q-proj to disable the model-specific default.

flags.name: --moe-data-parallel-size
flags.help: The moe data parallelism size.

flags.name: --pp-max-micro-batch-size
flags.help: The maximum micro batch size in pipeline parallelism.

flags.name: --pp-async-batch-depth
flags.help: The async batch depth of pipeline parallelism.

flags.name: --stream-interval
flags.help: The interval (or buffer size) for streaming in terms of the token length. A smaller value makes streaming smoother, while a larger value makes the throughput higher

flags.name: --incremental-streaming-output
flags.help: Whether to output as a sequence of disjoint segments.

flags.name: --random-seed
flags.help: The random seed.

flags.name: --mlx-enable-sampling
flags.help: MLX backend only: sample decode tokens (temperature / top-k / top-p / min-p) instead of greedy argmax. Sampling runs inside the lazy MLX graph, so it works with the overlap scheduler; first tokens from prefill/extend are sampled too. Greedy requests keep exact argmax behavior. Also enables on the MLX path: grammar vocab masks and custom logit processors (these break decode chaining per step; custom processors run on pure-decode steps only), logit_bias, output logprobs (sampled token / top-k / token_ids; prompt input logprobs are not computed), NaN sanitization (SGLANG_SANITIZE_NAN_LOGITS), and per-request sampling_seed under —enable-deterministic-inference (deterministic within MLX only). Penalties are not applied.

flags.name: --constrained-json-whitespace-pattern
flags.help: (outlines and llguidance backends only) Regex pattern for syntactic whitespaces allowed in JSON constrained output. For example, to allow the model to generate consecutive whitespaces, set the pattern to [\n\t ]*

flags.name: --constrained-json-disable-any-whitespace
flags.help: (xgrammar and llguidance backends only) Enforce compact representation in JSON constrained output.

flags.name: --watchdog-timeout
flags.help: Set watchdog timeout in seconds. If a forward batch takes longer than this, the server will crash to prevent hanging.

flags.name: --soft-watchdog-timeout
flags.help: Set soft watchdog timeout in seconds. If a forward batch takes longer than this, the server will dump information for debugging.

flags.name: --dist-timeout
flags.help: Set timeout for torch.distributed initialization.

flags.name: --download-dir
flags.help: Model download directory for huggingface.

flags.name: --model-checksum
flags.help: Model file integrity verification. If provided without value, uses model-path as HF repo ID. Otherwise, provide checksums JSON file path or HuggingFace repo ID.

flags.name: --base-gpu-id
flags.help: The base GPU ID to start allocating GPUs from. Useful when running multiple instances on the same machine.

flags.name: --gpu-id-step
flags.help: The delta between consecutive GPU IDs that are used. For example, setting it to 2 will use GPU 0,2,4,…

flags.name: --sleep-on-idle
flags.help: Reduce CPU usage when sglang is idle.

flags.name: --custom-sigquit-handler
flags.help: Register a custom sigquit handler so you can do additional cleanup after the server is shutdown. This is only available for Engine, not for CLI.

flags.name: --batch-notify-size
flags.help: Number of streaming notifications to batch before yielding to the event loop. Reduces asyncio wakeup overhead under high concurrency.

flags.name: --stream-response-default-include-usage
flags.help: Include usage in every streaming response (even when stream_options is not specified).

flags.name: --enable-streaming-session
flags.help: Enable streaming session mode and StreamingSession wrapper.

flags.name: --load-snapshot-publish-interval
flags.help: Publish load snapshot to shared memory every N decode iterations. Prefill and idle always publish immediately.

flags.name: --use-ray
flags.help: Use Ray actors for scheduler process management.

flags.name: --log-level
flags.help: The logging level of all loggers.

flags.name: --log-level-http
flags.help: The logging level of HTTP server. If not set, reuse —log-level by default.

flags.name: --log-requests
flags.help: Log metadata, inputs, outputs of all requests. The verbosity is decided by —log-requests-level

flags.name: --log-requests-level
flags.help: 0: Log metadata (no sampling parameters). 1: Log metadata and sampling parameters. 2: Log metadata, sampling parameters and partial input/output. 3: Log every input/output.

flags.name: --log-requests-format
flags.help: Format for request logging: ‘text’ (human-readable) or ‘json’ (structured)

flags.name: --log-requests-target
flags.help: Target(s) for request logging: ‘stdout’ and/or directory path(s) for file output. Can specify multiple targets, e.g., ‘—log-requests-target stdout /my/path’.

flags.name: --uvicorn-access-log-exclude-prefixes
flags.help: Exclude uvicorn access logs whose request path starts with any of these prefixes. Defaults to empty (disabled).

flags.name: --crash-dump-folder
flags.help: Folder for crash diagnostics. Stores completed requests retained by the crash-dump buffer plus in-flight requests and, on NVIDIA CUDA, configures device coredumps under this folder. Existing CUDA coredump environment variables take precedence. If not specified, this option does not enable request crash dumping or set CUDA coredump defaults.

flags.name: --show-time-cost
flags.help: Show time cost of custom marks.

flags.name: --enable-metrics
flags.help: Enable log prometheus metrics.

flags.name: --enable-mfu-metrics
flags.help: Enable estimated MFU-related prometheus metrics.

flags.name: --enable-metrics-for-all-schedulers
flags.help: Enable —enable-metrics-for-all-schedulers when you want schedulers on all TP ranks (not just TP 0) to record request metrics separately. This is especially useful when dp_attention is enabled, as otherwise all metrics appear to come from TP 0.

flags.name: --tokenizer-metrics-custom-labels-header
flags.help: Specify the HTTP header for passing custom labels for tokenizer metrics.

flags.name: --tokenizer-metrics-allowed-custom-labels
flags.help: The custom labels allowed for tokenizer metrics. The labels are specified via a dict in ‘—tokenizer-metrics-custom-labels-header’ field in HTTP requests, e.g., {‘label1’: ‘value1’, ‘label2’: ‘value2’} is allowed if ‘—tokenizer-metrics-allowed-custom-labels label1 label2’ is set.

flags.name: --bucket-time-to-first-token
flags.help: The buckets of time to first token, specified as a list of floats.

flags.name: --bucket-inter-token-latency
flags.help: The buckets of inter-token latency, specified as a list of floats.

flags.name: --bucket-e2e-request-latency
flags.help: The buckets of end-to-end request latency, specified as a list of floats.

flags.name: --prompt-tokens-buckets
flags.help: The buckets rule of prompt tokens. Supports 3 rule types: ‘default’ uses predefined buckets; ‘tse <middle> <base> <count>’ generates two sides exponential distributed buckets (e.g., ‘tse 1000 2 8’ generates buckets [984.0, 992.0, 996.0, 998.0, 1000.0, 1002.0, 1004.0, 1008.0, 1016.0]).); ‘custom <value1> <value2> …’ uses custom bucket values (e.g., ‘custom 10 50 100 500’).

flags.name: --generation-tokens-buckets
flags.help: The buckets rule for generation tokens histogram. Supports 3 rule types: ‘default’ uses predefined buckets; ‘tse <middle> <base> <count>’ generates two sides exponential distributed buckets (e.g., ‘tse 1000 2 8’ generates buckets [984.0, 992.0, 996.0, 998.0, 1000.0, 1002.0, 1004.0, 1008.0, 1016.0]).); ‘custom <value1> <value2> …’ uses custom bucket values (e.g., ‘custom 10 50 100 500’).

flags.name: --gc-warning-threshold-secs
flags.help: The threshold for long GC warning. If a GC takes longer than this, a warning will be logged. Set to 0 to disable.

flags.name: --decode-log-interval
flags.help: The log interval of decode batch.

flags.name: --enable-request-time-stats-logging
flags.help: Enable per request time stats logging

flags.name: --kv-events-config
flags.help: Config in json format for NVIDIA dynamo KV event publishing. Publishing will be enabled if this flag is used. Runtime-load publishing for load-aware routers is a separate opt-in; see --load-publish-endpoint.

flags.name: --load-publish-endpoint
flags.help: Opt in to the runtime-load PUB socket that load-aware routers subscribe to. Off by default (unset or off). Use auto to reserve the dp_size ports packed after the --kv-events-config range, or a wildcard-host TCP address (e.g. tcp://*:6000) to place it explicitly; rank r binds port+r and /server_info advertises the base under the kv_events block. Requires --kv-events-config; startup fails if set without one, not bindable, or overlapping the KV range. auto reserves 2*dp_size ports from the KV base — space co-hosted engines accordingly. The router-facing update cadence follows --load-snapshot-publish-interval, so a large value there also staleness-caps this feed.

flags.name: --enable-trace
flags.help: Enable opentelemetry trace

flags.name: --trace-modules
flags.help: Select the components to trace. Available options are ‘request’ and ‘mooncake’. Format: <module1 name>,<module2 name>,…

flags.name: --otlp-traces-endpoint
flags.help: Config opentelemetry collector endpoint if —enable-trace is set. format: <ip>:<port>

flags.name: --grpc-http-sidecar-port
flags.help: Port for the HTTP sidecar server in gRPC mode (—grpc-mode). Serves Prometheus metrics and profiling endpoints. Defaults to —port + 1. Not used in HTTP mode.

flags.name: --extra-metric-labels
flags.help: The custom labels for metrics. e.g. ’{“label1”: “value1”, “label2”: “value2”}‘

flags.name: --enable-forward-pass-metrics
flags.help: Enable per-iteration forward pass metrics via ZMQ IPC. External consumers (e.g. Dynamo planner) subscribe to the IPC endpoint exposed in server_args.forward_pass_metrics_ipc_name.

flags.name: --export-metrics-to-file
flags.help: Export performance metrics for each request to local file (e.g. for forwarding to external systems).

flags.name: --export-metrics-to-file-dir
flags.help: Directory path for writing performance metrics files (required when —export-metrics-to-file is enabled).

flags.name: --api-key
flags.help: Set API key of the server. It is also used in the OpenAI API compatible server.

flags.name: --admin-api-key
flags.help: Set admin API key for administrative/control endpoints (e.g., weights update, cache flush, /server_info). Endpoints marked as admin-only require Authorization: Bearer <admin_api_key> when this is set.

flags.name: --served-model-name
flags.help: Override the model name returned by the v1/models endpoint in OpenAI API server.

flags.name: --weight-version
flags.help: Version identifier for the model weights. Defaults to ‘default’ if not specified.

flags.name: --chat-template
flags.help: The builtin chat template name or the path of the chat template file. This is only used for OpenAI-compatible API server.

flags.name: --hf-chat-template-name
flags.help: When the HuggingFace tokenizer has multiple chat templates (e.g., ‘default’, ‘tool_use’, ‘rag’), specify which named template to use. If not set, the first available template is used.

flags.name: --default-chat-template-kwargs
flags.help: A JSON object used as defaults for chat_template_kwargs by Chat Completions, Responses, Anthropic-compatible requests, and chat tokenization. Direct Ollama and embedding paths do not consume these defaults. For ordinary template keys, explicit per-request values take precedence. Keys are specific to the selected model’s chat template; reasoning_effort is normalized separately.

flags.name: --completion-template
flags.help: The builtin completion template name or the path of the completion template file. This is only used for OpenAI-compatible API server. only for code completion currently.

flags.name: --file-storage-path
flags.help: The path of the file storage in backend.

flags.name: --enable-cache-report
flags.help: Return number of cached tokens in usage.prompt_tokens_details for each openai request.

flags.name: --reasoning-parser
flags.help: Specify the parser for reasoning models. Use auto to detect the parser from the model’s chat template.

flags.name: --tool-call-parser
flags.help: Specify the parser for handling tool-call interactions. Use auto to detect the parser from the model’s chat template.

flags.name: --tool-server
flags.help: Either ‘demo’ or a comma-separated list of tool server urls to use for the model. If not specified, no external tool server will be used. Native GPT-OSS web_search can still be enabled with EXA_API_KEY.

flags.name: --sampling-defaults
flags.help: Where to get default sampling parameters. ‘openai’ uses SGLang/OpenAI defaults (temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0, etc.). ‘model’ uses the model’s generation_config.json to get the recommended sampling parameters if available. Default is ‘model’.

flags.name: --strip-thinking-cache
flags.help: Skip caching reasoning-model output (thinking + answer) in the radix tree on finish; keep only the prompt prefix. Opt-in: changes cache contents.

flags.name: --enable-strict-thinking
flags.help: Enable strict token filtering during the thinking phase. Blocks model-specific excluded tokens (e.g., tool call markers) during reasoning. Requires a grammar backend that supports token filtering.

flags.name: --asr-max-buffer-seconds
flags.help: Maximum seconds of PCM audio the streaming ASR WebSocket handler will accumulate before closing the session with a buffer_overflow error. Guards against OOM when a client streams audio faster than inference can consume it. Default 60s.

flags.name: --asr-max-concurrent-sessions
flags.help: Maximum number of concurrent realtime ASR WebSocket sessions served by /v1/realtime. New connections beyond this cap are accepted, sent an error{code:too_many_sessions} frame, and closed. Default 32.

flags.name: --data-parallel-size
flags.help: The number of data-parallel replicas of the model.

flags.name: --attention-data-parallel-size
flags.help: The attention data parallelism size: the number of data-parallel attention groups inside the TP group, one scheduler each, while the FFN stays tensor parallel.

flags.name: --load-balance-method
flags.help: The load balancing strategy for data parallelism. The total_tokens algorithm can only be used when DP attention is applied. This algorithm performs load balancing based on the real-time token load of the DP workers.

flags.name: --dist-init-addr
flags.help: The host address for initializing distributed backend (e.g., 192.168.0.2:25000).

flags.name: --nnodes
flags.help: The number of nodes.

flags.name: --node-rank
flags.help: The node rank.

flags.name: --json-model-override-args
flags.help: A dictionary in JSON string format used to override default model configurations.

flags.name: --preferred-sampling-params
flags.help: json-formatted sampling settings that will be returned in /get_model_info

flags.name: --enable-lora
flags.help: Enable LoRA support for the model. This argument is automatically set to True if --lora-paths is provided for backward compatibility.

flags.name: --enable-lora-overlap-loading
flags.help: Enable asynchronous LoRA weight loading in order to overlap H2D transfers with GPU compute. This should be enabled if you find that your LoRA workloads are bottlenecked by adapter weight loading, for example when frequently loading large LoRA adapters.

flags.name: --max-lora-rank
flags.help: The maximum LoRA rank that should be supported. If not specified, it will be automatically inferred from the adapters provided in —lora-paths. This argument is needed when you expect to dynamically load adapters of larger LoRA rank after server startup.

flags.name: --lora-target-modules
flags.help: The union set of all target modules where LoRA should be applied (e.g., q_proj, k_proj, gate_proj). If not specified, it will be automatically inferred from the adapters provided in —lora-paths. You can also set it to all to enable LoRA for all supported modules; note this may introduce minor performance overhead.

flags.name: --lora-paths
flags.help: The list of LoRA adapters to load. Each adapter must be specified in one of the following formats: <PATH> | <NAME>=<PATH> | JSON with schema {“lora_name”: str, “lora_path”: str, “pinned”: bool}.

flags.name: --max-loras-per-batch
flags.help: Maximum number of adapters for a running batch, including base-only requests.

flags.name: --max-loaded-loras
flags.help: If specified, limits the maximum number of LoRA adapters loaded in CPU memory at a time. Must be ≥ —max-loras-per-batch.

flags.name: --lora-eviction-policy
flags.help: LoRA adapter eviction policy when the GPU memory pool is full.

flags.name: --lora-backend
flags.help: Choose the kernel backend for multi-LoRA serving.

flags.name: --max-lora-chunk-size
flags.help: Maximum chunk size for the ChunkedSGMV LoRA backend. Only used when —lora-backend is csgmv. Larger values may improve performance.

flags.name: --lora-drain-wait-threshold
flags.help: When any LoRA adapter request waits longer than this threshold (in seconds), the scheduler will selectively drain one running adapter to make room. This mitigates extreme tail latency under high or skewed workloads by preventing a small set of adapters from monopolizing batch slots. Set to 0 to disable draining (default).

flags.name: --experts-shared-outer-loras
flags.help: Force shared outer LoRA mode for MoE models. When set, w1/w3 lora_A and w2 lora_B are shared across experts (expert_dim=1). Use —no-experts-shared-outer-loras to force disable. By default this is auto-detected from adapter weights.

flags.name: --lora-use-virtual-experts
flags.help: Enable virtual expert computation for MoE models. When set, the model will use virtual expert computation.

flags.name: --lora-strict-loading
flags.help: Enable strict loading for LoRA adapters. When set, mismatched or missing keys in the adapter weights will raise an error.

flags.name: --attention-backend
flags.help: Choose the kernels for attention layers.

flags.name: --prefill-attention-backend
flags.help: Choose the kernels for prefill attention layers (have priority over —attention-backend).

flags.name: --decode-attention-backend
flags.help: Choose the kernels for decode attention layers (have priority over —attention-backend).

flags.name: --sampling-backend
flags.help: Choose the kernels for sampling layers.

flags.name: --grammar-backend
flags.help: Choose the backend for grammar-guided decoding.

flags.name: --mm-attention-backend
flags.help: Set multimodal attention backend.

flags.name: --dsa-prefill-backend
flags.help: DSA backend for the prefill stage (overrides --attention-backend when running DeepSeek DSA-style attention).

flags.name: --dsa-decode-backend
flags.help: DSA backend for the decode stage when running DeepSeek DSA-style attention. Overrides --attention-backend for decoding.

flags.name: --dsa-topk-backend
flags.help: Choose the DSA indexer top-k backend for the target model. The torch backend currently requires SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=false.

flags.name: --enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer
flags.help: Enable the experimental FP4 C4 indexer path for DeepSeek V4. When unset, SGLang keeps the default DeepSeek V4 indexer path. Requires SM100 GPUs with DeepGEMM FP4 indexer support.

flags.name: --fp8-gemm-backend
flags.help: Choose the runner backend for Blockwise FP8 GEMM operations. For MXFP8 dense GEMM, auto selects flashinfer_cutedsl when FlashInfer reports support (currently SM100/SM103), and otherwise selects flashinfer_cutlass on supported Blackwell GPUs. Options also include ‘deep_gemm’ (JIT-compiled), ‘flashinfer_trtllm’ (FlashInfer TRTLLM backend; SM100/SM103 only), ‘flashinfer_cutlass’ (FlashInfer CUTLASS backend), ‘flashinfer_cutedsl’ (FlashInfer CuTe DSL MXFP8 backend; SM100/SM103 only), ‘flashinfer_deepgemm’ (Hopper SM90 only, uses swapAB optimization for small M dimensions in decoding), ‘cutlass’ (optimal for SM120 GPUs), ‘triton’ (fallback, widely compatible), and ‘aiter’ (ROCm only).

flags.name: --fp4-gemm-backend
flags.help: Choose the runner backend for NVFP4 GEMM operations. Options: ‘auto’ (default; selects flashinfer_cutedsl on SM100, marlin on SM80-SM90, flashinfer_cutlass otherwise (including SM120)), ‘flashinfer_cutlass’ (FlashInfer CUTLASS backend), ‘flashinfer_cudnn’ (FlashInfer cuDNN backend, optimal on CUDA 13+ with cuDNN 9.15+), ‘flashinfer_cutedsl’ (FlashInfer CuTe DSL backend), ‘flashinfer_trtllm’ (FlashInfer TensorRT-LLM backend, requires different weight preparation with shuffling), ‘marlin’ (weight-only W4A16 fallback for SM80-SM90). Requires FlashInfer to be installed.

flags.name: --bf16-gemm-backend
flags.help: Choose the backend for unquantized BF16 GEMM operations. Options: auto (default; selects cutedsl on SM10x GPUs, except deterministic inference selects torch; otherwise uses cuBLAS via torch.nn.functional.linear), cutedsl (SGLang JIT CuTe DSL TGV BF16 GEMM on SM10x; dispatches between the CuTe DSL kernel and cuBLAS), torch (always uses cuBLAS via torch.nn.functional.linear).

flags.name: --disable-flashinfer-autotune
flags.help: Flashinfer autotune is enabled by default. Set this flag to disable the autotune.

flags.name: --flashinfer-autotune-skip-ops
flags.help: FlashInfer custom-op identifiers to skip during autotuning. See FlashInfer’s autotuning documentation. Skipped ops use the heuristic fallback. SGLang temporarily skips mxfp8_gemm by default due to an IMA.

flags.name: --radix-cache-backend
flags.help: Name of a radix-cache backend previously registered via register_radix_cache_backend. Omit this flag to use the built-in default cache selection chain.

flags.name: --speculative-algorithm
flags.help: Speculative algorithm.

flags.name: --speculative-draft-model-path
flags.help: The path of the draft model weights. This can be a local folder or a Hugging Face repo ID.

flags.name: --speculative-draft-model-revision
flags.help: The specific draft model version to use. It can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default version.

flags.name: --speculative-draft-load-format
flags.help: The format of the draft model weights to load. If not specified, will use the same format as --load-format. Use ‘dummy’ to initialize draft model weights with random values for profiling.

flags.name: --speculative-num-steps
flags.help: The number of steps sampled from draft model in Speculative Decoding.

flags.name: --speculative-eagle-topk
flags.help: The number of tokens sampled from the draft model in eagle2 each step.

flags.name: --speculative-num-draft-tokens
flags.help: The number of tokens sampled from the draft model in Speculative Decoding.

flags.name: --speculative-accept-threshold-single
flags.help: Accept a draft token if its probability in the target model is greater than this threshold.

flags.name: --speculative-accept-threshold-acc
flags.help: The accept probability of a draft token is raised from its target probability p to min(1, p / threshold_acc).

flags.name: --speculative-token-map
flags.help: The path of the draft model’s small vocab table.

flags.name: --speculative-attention-mode
flags.help: Attention backend for speculative decoding operations (both target verify and draft extend). Can be one of ‘prefill’ (default) or ‘decode’.

flags.name: --speculative-draft-attention-backend
flags.help: Attention backend for speculative decoding drafting.

flags.name: --speculative-dsa-topk-backend
flags.help: Choose the DSA indexer top-k backend for speculative draft workers. The torch backend currently requires SGLANG_DSA_FUSE_TOPK=false.

flags.name: --speculative-moe-runner-backend
flags.help: MOE backend for EAGLE speculative decoding, see --moe-runner-backend for options. Same as moe runner backend if unset.

flags.name: --speculative-moe-a2a-backend
flags.help: MOE A2A backend for EAGLE speculative decoding, see --moe-a2a-backend for options. Same as moe a2a backend if unset.

flags.name: --speculative-draft-model-quantization
flags.help: The quantization method for speculative model.

flags.name: --speculative-dflash-block-size
flags.help: DFLASH only. Block size (verify window length). Alias of —speculative-num-draft-tokens for DFLASH.

flags.name: --speculative-draft-window-size
flags.help: Sliding window size for the draft model. Honored by Llama EAGLE-3 (LlamaForCausalLMEagle3) and DFLASH only; other EAGLE-3 backends (e.g. MLA-based drafters) silently ignore it. For Llama EAGLE-3, the drafter only attends to the most recent N keys (verifier hidden states + its own outputs); the verifier is unaffected. For DFLASH, the draft worker keeps a recent target-token window in its local KV cache (paged backends may retain up to one extra page on the left for alignment). Default is full attention/context.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-min-bfs-breadth
flags.help: The minimum breadth for BFS (Breadth-First Search) in ngram speculative decoding.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-max-bfs-breadth
flags.help: The maximum breadth for BFS (Breadth-First Search) in ngram speculative decoding.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-match-type
flags.help: Ngram tree-building mode. BFS selects recency-based expansion and PROB selects frequency-based expansion. This setting is forwarded to the ngram cache implementation.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-max-trie-depth
flags.help: Maximum suffix length stored and matched by the ngram trie.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-capacity
flags.help: The cache capacity for ngram speculative decoding.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-external-corpus-path
flags.help: Path to an external JSONL corpus to pre-load into SAM at startup. Additional corpora can be added at runtime via POST /add_external_corpus.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-external-sam-budget
flags.help: Number of draft nodes reserved for the external SAM subtree in ngram speculative decoding.

flags.name: --speculative-ngram-external-corpus-max-tokens
flags.help: Fail startup if the tokenized external ngram corpus exceeds this many tokens. Tune this based on your CPU memory budget.

flags.name: --speculative-adaptive
flags.help: Enable adaptive speculative decoding that dynamically adjusts num_steps based on acceptance rate.

flags.name: --speculative-adaptive-config
flags.help: Path to a JSON config file for adaptive speculative decoding tuning knobs.

flags.name: --speculative-skip-dp-mlp-sync
flags.help: Skip the extra MLP sync that the scheduler performs before merging a new batch when speculative decoding + DP attention are both enabled.

flags.name: --enable-multi-layer-eagle
flags.help: Enable multi-layer Eagle speculative decoding.

flags.name: --expert-parallel-size
flags.help: The expert parallelism size.

flags.name: --moe-a2a-backend
flags.help: Select the backend for all-to-all communication for expert parallelism.

flags.name: --moe-runner-backend
flags.help: Choose the runner backend for MoE.

flags.name: --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision
flags.help: Choose the computation precision of flashinfer mxfp4 moe. On SM90, fp8 selects the Humming-style MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation path introduced by FlashInfer #3738 and requires FlashInfer >= 0.6.18.

flags.name: --enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion
flags.help: Enable FlashInfer allreduce fusion with Residual RMSNorm.

flags.name: --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion
flags.help: Enable aiter allreduce fusion with Residual RMSNorm.

flags.name: --deepep-mode
flags.help: Select the mode when enable DeepEP MoE, could be normal, low_latency or auto. Default is auto, which means low_latency for decode batch and normal for prefill batch.

flags.name: --deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype
flags.help: Select DeepEP dispatcher output dtype, could be bf16, fp8, int8 (only Ascend A2/A3 Series NPUs), nvfp4 or auto. Default is auto, which follows a priority order (server argument → deprecated env var → input_global_scale check → dispatcher_output_dtype from quant_config → flashinfer/cutlass backend → NPU BF16 default → GPU FP8 default).

flags.name: --ep-num-redundant-experts
flags.help: Allocate this number of redundant experts in expert parallel.

flags.name: --ep-dispatch-algorithm
flags.help: The algorithm to choose ranks for redundant experts in expert parallel.

flags.name: --init-expert-location
flags.help: Initial location of EP experts.

flags.name: --enable-eplb
flags.help: Enable EPLB algorithm

flags.name: --eplb-algorithm
flags.help: Chosen EPLB algorithm

flags.name: --eplb-rebalance-num-iterations
flags.help: Number of iterations to automatically trigger a EPLB re-balance.

flags.name: --eplb-rebalance-layers-per-chunk
flags.help: Number of layers to rebalance per forward pass.

flags.name: --eplb-min-rebalancing-utilization-threshold
flags.help: Minimum threshold for GPU average utilization to trigger EPLB rebalancing. Must be in the range [0.0, 1.0].

flags.name: --expert-distribution-recorder-mode
flags.help: Mode of expert distribution recorder.

flags.name: --expert-distribution-recorder-buffer-size
flags.help: Circular buffer size of expert distribution recorder. Set to -1 to denote infinite buffer.

flags.name: --expert-balancedness-report-mode
flags.help: Where to report expert balancedness.

flags.name: --deepep-config
flags.help: Tuned DeepEP config suitable for your own cluster. It can be either a string with JSON content or a file path.

flags.name: --moe-dense-tp-size
flags.help: TP size for MoE dense MLP layers. This flag is useful when, with large TP size, there are errors caused by weights in MLP layers having dimension smaller than the min dimension GEMM supports.

flags.name: --elastic-ep-backend
flags.help: Specify the collective communication backend for elastic EP. Currently supports ‘mooncake’.

flags.name: --enable-elastic-expert-backup
flags.help: Enable elastic EP backend to backup expert weights in DRAM feature. Currently supports ‘mooncake’.

flags.name: --mooncake-ib-device
flags.help: The InfiniBand devices for Mooncake Backend transfer, accepts multiple comma-separated devices (e.g., —mooncake-ib-device mlx5_0,mlx5_1). Default is None, which triggers automatic device detection when Mooncake Backend is enabled.

flags.name: --enable-waterfill
flags.help: Enable Waterfill: dispatch the fused shared expert as an extra routed expert slot to the least-loaded EP rank. Supports DeepEP and MegaMOE MoE A2A backends, implicitly enables shared-expert fusion, and supports --deepep-mode auto, normal, or low_latency when used with DeepEP. Use auto or low_latency for production DeepEP decode so CUDA graph remains enabled. Supported on DeepSeek-V3/R1 with EP >= 2. By default, Waterfill uses the static local-batch path; set SGLANG_DISABLE_STATIC_WATERFILL=1 to force dynamic Waterfill with runtime EP all-reduce.

flags.name: --flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend
flags.help: Enable FlashInfer allreduce fusion and choose backend. Defaults to auto. ‘auto’: choose mnnvl on SM90 single-node systems and SM100/SM103 single-node or multi-node systems; choose trtllm otherwise. ‘trtllm’: available on single-node systems only. ‘mnnvl’: available on SM90 single-node systems and SM100/SM103 single-node or multi-node systems via MNNVL fabric. Fuses allreduce with Residual + RMSNorm for supported MoE models.

flags.name: --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion
flags.help: Enforce disable FlashInfer allreduce fusion.

flags.name: --max-mamba-cache-size
flags.help: The maximum size of the mamba cache.

flags.name: --mamba-ssm-dtype
flags.help: The data type of the SSM states in mamba cache. If not set, read from the model config.

flags.name: --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding
flags.help: Enable stochastic rounding when writing FP16 Mamba SSM cache states. Requires —mamba-ssm-dtype float16 and CUDA. With —mamba-backend triton, requires SM100.

flags.name: --mamba-cache-philox-rounds
flags.help: Number of Philox rounds to use for stochastic rounding of FP16 Mamba SSM cache writes. Triton uses the Triton default when set to 0; FlashInfer uses 10 rounds when set to 0.

flags.name: --mamba-full-memory-ratio
flags.help: The ratio of mamba state memory to full kv cache memory.

flags.name: --mamba-radix-cache-strategy
flags.help: The strategy to use for mamba scheduler. auto currently defaults to no_buffer. 1. no_buffer does not support overlap scheduler due to not allocating extra mamba state buffers. Branching point caching support is feasible but not implemented. 2. extra_buffer supports overlap schedule by allocating extra mamba state buffers to track mamba state for caching (mamba state usage per running req becomes 2x for non-spec; 1+(1/(2+speculative_num_draft_tokens))x for spec dec (e.g. 1.16x if speculative_num_draft_tokens==4)). 2a. extra_buffer is strictly better for non-KV-cache-bound cases; for KV-cache-bound cases, the tradeoff depends on whether enabling overlap outweighs reduced max running requests. 2b. mamba caching at radix cache branching point is strictly better than non-branch but requires kernel support, currently only extra_buffer supports branching. 3. extra_buffer_lazy lowers extra_buffer’s slot cost by allocating one track slot per request instead of two; the second slot is allocated on demand at track-interval boundaries (for speculative decoding it is reserved ahead of each verify window and committed only for accepted boundary crossings). Compatible with speculative decoding (EAGLE/NGRAM/DSPARK/DFLASH); not supported under PD disaggregation.

flags.name: --mamba-track-interval
flags.help: The interval (in tokens) to track the mamba state during decode. Only used when —mamba-radix-cache-strategy is extra_buffer. Must be divisible by page_size if set, and must be >= speculative_num_draft_tokens when using speculative decoding.

flags.name: --enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint
flags.help: Store radix-cached linear-attn (mamba) states in int8 (separate checkpoint pool) for ~2x cached-prefix capacity at fixed memory.

flags.name: --int8-mamba-ckpt-size
flags.help: Number of int8 mamba checkpoint slots (default: 2x the active mamba pool size).

flags.name: --mamba-backend
flags.help: Choose the kernel backend for Mamba SSM operations. Default is ‘triton’. Options: ‘triton’ (default), ‘flashinfer’ (requires FlashInfer with Mamba support).

flags.name: --linear-attn-backend
flags.help: The default kernel backend for linear attention (GDN/KDA). Can be overridden per-mode by —linear-attn-decode-backend and —linear-attn-prefill-backend.

flags.name: --linear-attn-decode-backend
flags.help: Override the kernel backend for linear attention decode. If not set, uses —linear-attn-backend.

flags.name: --linear-attn-prefill-backend
flags.help: Override the kernel backend for linear attention prefill/extend. If not set, uses —linear-attn-backend.

flags.name: --enable-hierarchical-cache
flags.help: Enable hierarchical cache

flags.name: --hicache-ratio
flags.help: The ratio of the size of host KV cache memory pool to the size of device pool.

flags.name: --hicache-size
flags.help: The size of host KV cache memory pool in gigabytes, which will override the hicache_ratio if set.

flags.name: --hicache-write-policy
flags.help: The write policy of hierarchical cache.

flags.name: --hicache-io-backend
flags.help: The IO backend for KV cache transfer between CPU and GPU

flags.name: --hicache-mem-layout
flags.help: The layout of host memory pool for hierarchical cache.

flags.name: --hicache-storage-backend
flags.help: The storage backend for hierarchical KV cache. Built-in backends: file, mooncake, hf3fs, nixl, aibrix. For dynamic backend, use —hicache-storage-backend-extra-config to specify: backend_name (custom name), module_path (Python module path), class_name (backend class name).

flags.name: --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy
flags.help: Control when prefetching from the storage backend should stop.

flags.name: --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config
flags.help: A dictionary in JSON string format, or a string starting with a @ followed by a config file in JSON/YAML/TOML format, containing extra configuration for the storage backend.

flags.name: --hisparse-config
flags.help: A dictionary in JSON string format for hierarchical sparse attention configuration. Required fields: algorithm (str), backend (str). All other fields are algorithm-specific and passed to the algorithm constructor.

flags.name: --enable-hisparse
flags.help: Enable hierarchical sparse attention

flags.name: --enable-lmcache
flags.help: Using LMCache as an alternative hierarchical cache solution

flags.name: --lmcache-config-file
flags.help: Path to the LMCache YAML configuration file

flags.name: --kt-weight-path
flags.help: [ktransformers parameter] The path of the quantized expert weights for amx kernel. A local folder.

flags.name: --kt-method
flags.help: [ktransformers parameter] Quantization formats for CPU execution.

flags.name: --kt-cpuinfer
flags.help: [ktransformers parameter] The number of CPUInfer threads.

flags.name: --kt-threadpool-count
flags.help: [ktransformers parameter] One-to-one with the number of NUMA nodes (one thread pool per NUMA).

flags.name: --kt-num-gpu-experts
flags.help: [ktransformers parameter] The number of GPU experts.

flags.name: --kt-max-deferred-experts-per-token
flags.help: [ktransformers parameter] Maximum number of experts deferred to CPU per token. All MoE layers except the final one use this value; the final layer always uses 0.

flags.name: --dllm-algorithm
flags.help: The diffusion LLM algorithm, such as LowConfidence.

flags.name: --dllm-algorithm-config
flags.help: The diffusion LLM algorithm configurations. Must be a YAML file.

flags.name: --dllm-fdfo
flags.help: First-Done-First-Out (FDFO) scheduling lets completed requests leave the batch immediately instead of waiting for slower requests, eliminating head-of-line blocking. Enabled by default; pass --no-dllm-fdfo to fall back to synchronous lockstep scheduling. Works with any dLLM algorithm.

flags.name: --cpu-offload-gb
flags.help: How many GBs of RAM to reserve for CPU offloading.

flags.name: --offload-group-size
flags.help: Number of layers per group in offloading.

flags.name: --ple-offload-embedding
flags.help: Keep the Qwen4-Exp PLE n-gram embedding table in host memory instead of device memory; the gather kernel reads it from a host pointer. Enabled by default for BF16 Qwen4-Exp on CUDA; --no-ple-offload-embedding disables it.

flags.name: --ple-offload-backend
flags.help: Host storage for the offloaded PLE table: pinned (CPU pinned memory) or file (a sparse file-backed mmap under --ple-offload-dir, read directly by the gather kernel). Use file on unified-memory devices such as GB10 / DGX Spark, where pinned host memory comes out of the same pool as the weights; it requires a device that reports cudaDevAttrPageableMemoryAccessUsesHostPageTables.

flags.name: --ple-offload-dir
flags.help: Directory for the file-backed PLE table when --ple-offload-backend is file. The file is sparse and rewritten on every startup; keep it on fast local storage (NVMe). Rewriting an existing table can be much slower than filling a fresh sparse file. Before restarting, stop all servers using that directory and remove its ple_table_*.bin files to avoid this startup cost.

flags.name: --offload-num-in-group
flags.help: Number of layers to be offloaded within a group.

flags.name: --offload-prefetch-step
flags.help: Steps to prefetch in offloading.

flags.name: --offload-mode
flags.help: Mode of offloading.

flags.name: --enable-mis
flags.help: Enable Multi-Item Scoring optimization. Combines query and multiple items into a single sequence for efficient batch processing. Requires —attention-backend flashinfer; auto-disables CUDA graph, radix cache, and chunked prefill.

flags.name: --disable-radix-cache
flags.help: Disable RadixAttention for prefix caching.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-config
flags.help: Canonical per-phase CUDA graph settings as JSON, e.g. . JSON wins over the per-phase —cuda-graph-* convenience flags and over the legacy flags. Allowed backends: full, breakable, tc_piecewise, disabled (full is decode-only).

flags.name: --cuda-graph-backend-decode
flags.help: Backend for the decode phase. Folds into cuda_graph_config[decode].backend.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-backend-prefill
flags.help: Backend for the prefill phase. Folds into cuda_graph_config[prefill].backend.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode
flags.help: Maximum batch size captured for the decode CUDA graph.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill
flags.help: Maximum batch size captured for the prefill CUDA graph.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-max-seq-len-prefill
flags.help: Longest sequence a prefill CUDA graph replay admits; longer batches run eager prefill. Folds into cuda_graph_config[prefill].max_seq_len.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-bs-decode
flags.help: Explicit list of batch sizes to capture for the decode CUDA graph.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-bs-prefill
flags.help: Explicit list of batch sizes to capture for the prefill CUDA graph.

flags.name: --cuda-graph-tc-compiler
flags.help: Compiler used by the tc_piecewise backend (only the prefill phase consumes it today).

flags.name: --disable-cuda-graph-padding
flags.help: Disable cuda graph when padding is needed. Still uses cuda graph when padding is not needed.

flags.name: --enable-profile-cuda-graph
flags.help: Enable profiling of cuda graph capture.

flags.name: --debug-cuda-graph
flags.help: Eager-mode CUDA graph via the breakable backend: graph breaks let every op run eagerly while still going through the capture/replay path. Useful for debugging capture/replay issues.

flags.name: --enable-cudagraph-gc
flags.help: Enable garbage collection during CUDA graph capture. If disabled (default), GC is frozen during capture to speed up the process.

flags.name: --enable-layerwise-nvtx-marker
flags.help: Enable layerwise NVTX profiling annotations for the model. This adds NVTX markers to every layer for detailed per-layer performance analysis with Nsight Systems.

flags.name: --enable-nccl-nvls
flags.help: Enable NCCL NVLS for prefill heavy requests when available.

flags.name: --enable-symm-mem
flags.help: Enable NCCL symmetric memory for fast collectives.

flags.name: --disable-flashinfer-cutlass-moe-fp4-allgather
flags.help: Disables quantize before all-gather for flashinfer cutlass moe.

flags.name: --enable-tokenizer-batch-encode
flags.help: Enable batch tokenization for improved performance when processing multiple text inputs. Do not use with image inputs, pre-tokenized input_ids, or input_embeds.

flags.name: --disable-tokenizer-batch-decode
flags.help: Disable batch decoding when decoding multiple completions.

flags.name: --disable-outlines-disk-cache
flags.help: Disable disk cache of outlines to avoid possible crashes related to file system or high concurrency.

flags.name: --disable-custom-all-reduce
flags.help: Disable the custom all-reduce kernel and fall back to NCCL.

flags.name: --enable-mscclpp
flags.help: Enable using mscclpp for small messages for all-reduce kernel and fall back to NCCL.

flags.name: --enable-torch-symm-mem
flags.help: Enable using torch symm mem for all-reduce kernel and fall back to NCCL. Only supports CUDA device SM90 and above. SM90 supports world size 4, 6, 8. SM10 supports world size 6, 8.

flags.name: --disable-overlap-schedule
flags.help: Disable the overlap scheduler, which overlaps the CPU scheduler with GPU model worker.

flags.name: --enable-mixed-chunk
flags.help: Enabling mixing prefill and decode in a batch when using chunked prefill.

flags.name: --enable-dp-attention
flags.help: Deprecated. Use —attn-dp-size <dp-size> instead of —dp-size <dp-size> —enable-dp-attention.

flags.name: --enable-dp-lm-head
flags.help: Enable vocabulary parallel across the attention TP group to avoid all-gather across DP groups, optimizing performance under DP attention.

flags.name: --enable-two-batch-overlap
flags.help: Enabling two micro batches to overlap.

flags.name: --enable-single-batch-overlap
flags.help: Let computation and communication overlap within one micro batch.

flags.name: --tbo-token-distribution-threshold
flags.help: The threshold of token distribution between two batches in micro-batch-overlap, determines whether to two-batch-overlap or two-chunk-overlap. Set to 0 denote disable two-chunk-overlap.

flags.name: --enable-torch-compile
flags.help: Optimize the model with torch.compile. Experimental feature.

flags.name: --enable-torch-compile-debug-mode
flags.help: Enable debug mode for torch compile.

flags.name: --torch-compile-max-bs
flags.help: Set the maximum batch size when using torch compile.

flags.name: --disable-cuda-graph
flags.help: Deprecated. Use —cuda-graph-backend-decode=disabled and/or —cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled.

flags.name: --disable-prefill-cuda-graph
flags.help: Disable the prefill-phase CUDA graph. Convenience for —cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled.

flags.name: --disable-decode-cuda-graph
flags.help: Disable the decode-phase CUDA graph. Convenience for —cuda-graph-backend-decode=disabled.

flags.name: --enable-p2p-check
flags.help: Enable P2P check for GPU access, otherwise the p2p access is allowed by default.

flags.name: --triton-attention-reduce-in-fp32
flags.help: Cast the intermediate attention results to fp32 to avoid possible crashes related to fp16. This only affects Triton attention kernels.

flags.name: --triton-attention-num-kv-splits
flags.help: The number of KV splits in flash decoding Triton kernel. Larger value is better in longer context scenarios. The default value is 8.

flags.name: --triton-attention-split-tile-size
flags.help: The size of split KV tile in flash decoding Triton kernel. Used for deterministic inference.

flags.name: --num-continuous-decode-steps
flags.help: Run multiple continuous decoding steps to reduce scheduling overhead. This can potentially increase throughput but may also increase time-to-first-token latency. The default value is 1, meaning only run one decoding step at a time.

flags.name: --delete-ckpt-after-loading
flags.help: Delete the model checkpoint after loading the model.

flags.name: --enable-memory-saver
flags.help: Allow saving memory using release_memory_occupation and resume_memory_occupation

flags.name: --enable-weights-cpu-backup
flags.help: Save model weights to CPU memory during release_weights_occupation and resume_weights_occupation

flags.name: --enable-draft-weights-cpu-backup
flags.help: Save draft model weights to CPU memory during release_weights_occupation and resume_weights_occupation

flags.name: --allow-auto-truncate
flags.help: Allow automatically truncating requests that exceed the maximum input length instead of returning an error.

flags.name: --enable-custom-logit-processor
flags.help: Enable users to pass custom logit processors to the server (disabled by default for security)

flags.name: --flashinfer-mla-disable-ragged
flags.help: Not using ragged prefill wrapper when running flashinfer mla

flags.name: --disable-shared-experts-fusion
flags.help: Disable shared experts fusion optimization for deepseek v3/r1.

flags.name: --disable-chunked-prefix-cache
flags.help: Disable chunked prefix cache feature for deepseek, which should save overhead for short sequences.

flags.name: --image-processor-backend
flags.help: Image processor backend. auto lets Transformers select the best available backend.

flags.name: --disable-fast-image-processor
flags.help: Deprecated. Use --image-processor-backend=pil instead.

flags.name: --enable-return-hidden-states
flags.help: Enable returning hidden states with responses.

flags.name: --return-hidden-states-mode
flags.help: Set the maximum hidden-state return mode supported by the server. last allows requests with return_hidden_states=False or last; full also allows return_hidden_states=True.

flags.name: --enable-return-routed-experts
flags.help: Enable returning routed experts of each layer with responses.

flags.name: --scheduler-recv-interval
flags.help: The interval to poll requests in scheduler. Can be set to >1 to reduce the overhead of this.

flags.name: --numa-node
flags.help: Sets the numa node for the subprocesses. i-th element corresponds to i-th subprocess.

flags.name: --enable-deterministic-inference
flags.help: Enable deterministic inference mode with batch invariant ops.

flags.name: --rl-on-policy-target
flags.help: The training system that SGLang needs to match for true on-policy.

flags.name: --enable-attn-tp-input-scattered
flags.help: Allow input of attention to be scattered when only using tensor parallelism, to reduce the computational load of operations such as qkv latent.

flags.name: --enable-prefill-cp
flags.help: Enable context parallelism for the prefill phase. Select the layout with —cp-strategy.

flags.name: --cp-strategy
flags.help: Sharding strategy for prefill CP. zigzag assigns each rank one early and one late sequence block; interleave assigns token indices modulo the CP size.

flags.name: --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope
flags.help: Enable fused qk normalization and rope rotary embedding.

flags.name: --enable-precise-embedding-interpolation
flags.help: Enable corner alignment for resize of embeddings grid to ensure more accurate(but slower) evaluation of interpolated embedding values.

flags.name: --kv-canary
flags.help: KV cache canary mode. ‘none’ disables the canary (default). ‘log’ prints them while the server keeps running (production-safe). ‘raise’ fails the server on the first detected mismatch (CI lane).

flags.name: --kv-canary-real-data
flags.help: Check the real KV-cache in the canary. ‘none’ (default) disables the feature. ‘partial’ checks the first 16 bytes of each real-KV slot. ‘all’ checks the full real-KV slot.

flags.name: --kv-canary-sweep-interval
flags.help: Every N forward steps, run a full-pool sweep.

flags.name: --pre-warm-nccl
flags.help: Pre-warm NCCL/RCCL communicators during startup to reduce P99 TTFT cold-start latency. Default: enabled for AMD/HIP (RCCL), disabled for NVIDIA/CUDA (NCCL).

flags.name: --enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast
flags.help: With DP-attention, send control messages to every DP group leader and broadcast within attn_tp_group instead of the full tp_group. Eliminates a costly all-ranks gloo sync on every scheduler iteration.

flags.name: --enforce-shared-experts-fusion
flags.help: Enforce shared experts fusion even when it would normally be disabled (e.g. under DeepEP). Mutually exclusive with —disable-shared-experts-fusion.

flags.name: --enable-return-indexer-topk
flags.help: Enable returning indexer topk indices of layers with indexer with responses.

flags.name: --disable-attn-tp-gather
flags.help: Disable scheduler-side attn_tp_gather (the upstream SP path that pads num_tokens to attn_tp_size and pre-allocates a gathered buffer). Use for models that manage SP scatter/gather at the model level (e.g., perform their own all_gather/reduce_scatter inside attention) and do not consume the upstream gathered_buffer. Without this, the cuda graph runner pads num_tokens to attn_tp_size, which can cause kernel autotuners to select wrong-sized variants at small batches.

flags.name: --enable-fused-moe-sum-all-reduce
flags.help: Enable fused moe triton and sum all reduce.

flags.name: --gc-threshold
flags.help: Set the garbage collection thresholds (the collection frequency). Accepts 1 to 3 integers.

flags.name: --enable-dynamic-batch-tokenizer
flags.help: Enable async dynamic batch tokenizer for improved performance when multiple requests arrive concurrently.

flags.name: --dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-size
flags.help: [Only used if —enable-dynamic-batch-tokenizer is set] Maximum batch size for dynamic batch tokenizer.

flags.name: --dynamic-batch-tokenizer-batch-timeout
flags.help: [Only used if —enable-dynamic-batch-tokenizer is set] Timeout in seconds for batching tokenization requests.

flags.name: --debug-tensor-dump-output-folder
flags.help: The output folder for dumping tensors.

flags.name: --debug-tensor-dump-layers
flags.help: The layer ids to dump. Dump all layers if not specified.

flags.name: --debug-tensor-dump-input-file
flags.help: The input filename for dumping tensors

flags.name: --debug-tensor-dump-inject
flags.help: Inject the outputs from jax as the input of every layer.

flags.name: --disaggregation-mode
flags.help: Only used for PD disaggregation. “prefill” for prefill-only server, and “decode” for decode-only server. If not specified, it is not PD disaggregated

flags.name: --disaggregation-transfer-backend
flags.help: The backend for disaggregation transfer. Default is mooncake.

flags.name: --disaggregation-bootstrap-port
flags.help: Bootstrap server port on the prefill server. Default is 8998.

flags.name: --disaggregation-ib-device
flags.help: The InfiniBand devices for disaggregation transfer, accepts single device (e.g., —disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0) or multiple comma-separated devices (e.g., —disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0,mlx5_1). Default is None, which triggers automatic device detection when mooncake backend is enabled.

flags.name: --disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache
flags.help: Enable async KV cache offloading on decode server (PD mode).

flags.name: --num-reserved-decode-tokens
flags.help: Number of decode tokens that will have memory reserved when adding new request to the running batch.

flags.name: --disaggregation-decode-polling-interval
flags.help: The interval to poll requests in decode server. Can be set to >1 to reduce the overhead of this.

flags.name: --disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache
flags.help: Enable radix cache on decode server (PD mode). Caches KV prefixes to avoid redundant transfers. Incompatible with —enable-hisparse, speculative decoding, and —disaggregation-transfer-backend fake.

flags.name: --optimistic-prefill-retries
flags.help: Number of optimistic prefill retries that will skip the bootstrap wait.

flags.name: --encoder-only
flags.help: For MLLM with an encoder, launch an encoder-only server

flags.name: --language-only
flags.help: For VLM, load weights for the language model only.

flags.name: --language-model-only
flags.help: Skip the multimodal encoder entirely: its weights are never loaded and the tower is never built, freeing that GPU memory for KV cache. Multimodal requests are rejected. Unlike —language-only this is a standalone mode, not part of encoder/decoder disaggregation.

flags.name: --encoder-transfer-backend
flags.help: The backend for encoder disaggregation transfer. Default is zmq_to_scheduler.

flags.name: --encoder-urls
flags.help: List of encoder server urls.

flags.name: --encoder-bootstrap-port
flags.help: Port for the EncoderBootstrapServer that runs in the language-only tokenizer manager process. Encoders register here, and language-only receivers fetch the current URL list from here.

flags.name: --encoder-register-urls
flags.help: One or more EncoderBootstrapServer URLs to register this encoder with on startup, for dynamic encoder discovery. Example: —encoder-register-urls http://prefill0:8997 http://prefill1:8997. Used with —encoder-only servers.

flags.name: --enable-adaptive-dispatch-to-encoder
flags.help: When enabled, adaptively dispatch: multi-image requests go to encoder in language_only epd mode, single-image requests are processed locally.

flags.name: --custom-weight-loader
flags.help: The custom dataloader which used to update the model. Should be set with a valid import path, such as my_package.weight_load_func

flags.name: --weight-loader-disable-mmap
flags.help: Disable mmap while loading weight using safetensors.

flags.name: --weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints
flags.help: Prefetch checkpoint files into OS page cache before loading. Each rank prefetches a fraction of the shards in a background thread, reducing total network I/O on shared filesystems (NFS/Lustre) from N*checkpoint to 1*checkpoint. Recommended for models on network storage. When enabled, multi-threaded safetensors loading is disabled by default to avoid I/O oversubscription with the prefetch threads; set enable_multithread_load=true in --model-loader-extra-config to keep multi-threaded loading (e.g. on local NVMe where prefetch is a no-op).

flags.name: --weight-loader-prefetch-num-threads
flags.help: Number of threads per rank for checkpoint prefetching.

flags.name: --remote-instance-weight-loader-seed-instance-ip
flags.help: The ip of the seed instance for loading weights from remote instance.

flags.name: --remote-instance-weight-loader-seed-instance-service-port
flags.help: The service port of the seed instance for loading weights from remote instance.

flags.name: --remote-instance-weight-loader-send-weights-group-ports
flags.help: The communication group ports for loading weights from remote instance.

flags.name: --remote-instance-weight-loader-backend
flags.help: The backend for loading weights from remote instance. Can be ‘transfer_engine’, ‘nccl’, or ‘modelexpress’. Default is ‘nccl’.

flags.name: --remote-instance-weight-loader-start-seed-via-transfer-engine
flags.help: Start seed server via transfer engine backend for remote instance weight loader.

flags.name: --weight-loader-drop-cache-after-load
flags.help: Call posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) on each safetensors shard after loading it.

flags.name: --engine-info-bootstrap-port
flags.help: Port for the engine info bootstrap server. Default is 6789. Must be set explicitly when running multiple instances on the same node.

flags.name: --modelexpress-config
flags.help: JSON config for ModelExpress P2P weight loading. Keys: “url” (optional gRPC host:port override), “transport” (“nixl” or “transfer_engine”). Example: ’{“url”: “localhost:8001”, “transport”: “nixl”}‘

flags.name: --enable-pdmux
flags.help: Enable PD-Multiplexing, PD running on greenctx stream.

flags.name: --pdmux-config-path
flags.help: The path of the PD-Multiplexing config file.

flags.name: --sm-group-num
flags.help: Number of sm partition groups.

flags.name: --config
flags.help: Read CLI options from a config file. Must be a YAML file with configuration options.

flags.name: --enable-broadcast-mm-inputs-process
flags.help: Enable broadcast mm-inputs process in scheduler.

flags.name: --mm-process-config
flags.help: Multimodal preprocessing config, a json config contains keys: image, video, audio.

flags.name: --allowed-media-domains
flags.help: Restrict client-supplied HTTP(S) media URLs and redirect destinations to these exact hostnames.

flags.name: --media-url-max-file-size-mb
flags.help: Maximum streamed size in MiB for one remote media download. Set to 0 to disable the limit.

flags.name: --mm-enable-dp-encoder
flags.help: Enabling data parallelism for mm encoder. The dp size will be set to the tp size automatically.

flags.name: --limit-mm-data-per-request
flags.help: Limit the number of multimodal inputs per request. e.g. ’{“image”: 1, “video”: 1, “audio”: 1}‘

flags.name: --enable-mm-global-cache
flags.help: Enable Mooncake-backed global multimodal embedding cache on encoder servers so repeated images can reuse cached ViT embeddings instead of recomputing them.

flags.name: --decrypted-config-file
flags.help: The path of the decrypted config file.

flags.name: --decrypted-draft-config-file
flags.help: The path of the decrypted draft config file.

flags.name: --enable-prefix-mm-cache
flags.help: Enable prefix multimodal cache. Currently only supports mm-only.

flags.name: --forward-hooks
flags.help: JSON-formatted list of forward hook specifications. Each element must include target_modules (list of glob patterns matched against model.named_modules() names) and hook_factory (Python import path to a factory, e.g. my_package.hooks:make_hook). An optional name field is used for logging, and an optional config object is passed as a dict to the factory.

flags.name: --msprobe-dump-config
flags.help: The path of the JSON configuration file for msProbe. If specified, enables msProbe dump.

flags.name: --hybrid-kvcache-ratio
flags.help: Mix ratio in [0,1] between uniform and hybrid kv buffers (0.0 = pure uniform: swa_size / full_size = 1)(1.0 = pure hybrid: swa_size / full_size = local_attention_size / context_length)
